A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MVGenMaster and MvD-1M. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support matching retained, moved and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original novel-view synthesis, 3D reconstruction, scalability and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds the authors' reconstruction results on the Reconfusion benchmark and further key-rescaling ablations.

M1.justification: The SD2 backbone, warped RGB and CCM priors, cross-view attention, training modifications and constant-gamma key-rescaling method remain. The expanded CNN and CCM descriptions clarify implementation; the adaptive rescaling alternatives are ablation comparisons, not replacements for the proposed method.

E1.justification: v3 Table 10 extends reconstruction evaluation to Real10k and CO3D. These datasets already appeared in v1's training and NVS evaluations, but its reconstruction benchmark covered Tanks-and-Temples, DTU and MipNeRF-360. Training dataset coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: v3 Table 10 substantially extends reconstruction comparisons by adding published results for Reconfusion and original CAT3D, distinct from the CAT3D* reimplementation retained in Tables 2–3. Table 13 also evaluates attention-entropy-based adaptive rescaling alternatives A1 and A2.

E3.justification: The added reconstruction experiment uses Reconfusion's official splits and 3-, 6- and 9-reference-view settings; v3 explicitly distinguishes its MipNeRF-360 split from Table 3. Table 13 adds controlled reference/target-count and gamma configurations. Existing main experiments and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 already included gamma sensitivity at 158 total views. v3 Table 13 extends this analysis to different reference/target counts and compares fixed gamma with two adaptive alternatives, testing reference scarcity and sequence-length dependence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added tables retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained, including v1 Tables 10–12, which become v3 Tables 11, 12 and 14. New Tables 10 and 13 add substantial reconstruction and rescaling findings. For example, the new nine-view Real10k comparison reports MVGenMaster PSNR/LPIPS of 27.54/0.062 versus CAT3D's 32.20/0.082. These are additional comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v3 Equation 5 explicitly writes the camera-to-world unprojection underlying the CCM already described in v1 Section 3.1. It supplies mathematical exposition without changing the underlying reasoning or adding a theorem, proof or substantive formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: 3D-prior-enhanced generalization, flexible multi-view generation, key-rescaling and the 1.6-million-scene MvD-1M dataset. The 158-view capability mentioned more prominently in v3 was already demonstrated in v1's appendix.

C2.justification: v3 adds qualifications about reconstruction pipeline and split differences, weaker key-rescaling benefits with one reference view, sequence-length dependence and unresolved optimal-gamma selection. The background-artifact limitation and proposed DiT/rendering extensions already appeared in v1; their relocation is not a new limitation.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies VAE versus independently trained CNN input encoding, details CCM construction and normalization to 0–1, and discloses Dust3R point-cloud initialization for 3DGS. It also adds a combined reconstruction runtime and project-page access information for code, models and data. These disclosures do not establish changes to existing experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Zip-NeRF and Jin et al.'s training-free diffusion adaptation work, supporting reconstruction and adaptive-rescaling discussions. It expands comparison positioning against already-cited CAT3D and Reconfusion. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 consolidates NVS and reconstruction under Section 4.1, renumbers the ablation section, moves the concluding limitations paragraph into Appendix D, and adds focused implementation and experimental explanations. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 10 and 13, redraws Figure 2's input-processing paths, enlarges and simplifies Figure 4, shortens Figure 7's examples, and places Figures 5–6 together. Appendix tables and figures are rearranged; most visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: The implementation clarifications improve reproducibility, while comparisons with original CAT3D/Reconfusion and expanded rescaling ablations make the evidence more informative than v1's reliance on CAT3D* and narrower sensitivity tests. The gains are limited: reconstruction pipelines differ, and the new description of PSNR as comparable understates some Real10k gaps. Overall, the added evidence and clearer documentation provide a modest net improvement.
